name: Belfast City Hall
description: Belfast’s domed city hall, finished in 1906, in the middle of Donegall Square, with free tours and an exhibition on the city’s history.

name: Crown Liquor Saloon
places: Crown Liquor Saloon, Great Victoria Street
description: A Victorian pub opposite the Europa Hotel, with gas lamps, coloured tiles and carved wooden snugs. It is owned by the National Trust.

name: Titanic Belfast
description: A museum on the story of the Titanic, at the head of the slipways where the ship was built. The slipways are now an open plaza.

name: Harland & Wolff Drawing Offices
description: The shipyard offices where the Titanic and her sister ships were designed, now part of the Titanic Hotel. The tall drawing halls survive.

name: Divis Tower
description: A 20-storey tower at the foot of the Falls Road, the only block left of the 1960s Divis Flats estate. The army kept a post on its roof.

name: Cupar Way peace wall
description: A high wall of concrete and steel between the Catholic Falls and Protestant Shankill areas, covered in murals and visitors’ messages.

name: Parliament Buildings, Stormont
description: Northern Ireland’s parliament, a white neoclassical building at the top of a long drive on the Stormont estate. It is open for tours.

name: Europa Hotel
description: A city-centre hotel opened in 1971 and bombed many times during the Troubles, often called the most bombed hotel in Europe.

name: Cultúrlann McAdam Ó Fiaich
places: Cultúrlann McAdam Ó Fiaich, Falls Road
description: An Irish-language arts centre in a former church on the Falls Road, with a café, a bookshop and a theatre.

name: Queen’s University Belfast
description: Belfast’s main university, founded in 1845. Its red-brick Lanyon Building faces University Road, and the students’ union hosts gigs.
